Let’s go through each option step by step.  

**(A) The suspensor is derived from the basal cell.**  
In plant embryogenesis, after the zygote divides, it forms a basal cell and an apical cell. The basal cell typically gives rise to the suspensor, so this is correct.  

**(B) Cotyledons are derived from the apical cell.**  
The apical cell develops into the embryo proper, which includes the cotyledons, so this is correct.  

**(C) Shoot apical meristem formation occurs after seed formation.**  
This is suspicious. In embryogenesis, the shoot apical meristem (SAM) actually forms during embryogenesis, before seed formation is complete. Seeds contain a mature embryo with SAM already present at germination. So saying SAM forms *after* seed formation is incorrect.  

**(D) Precursors of all three plant tissue systems are formed during embryogenesis.**  
The three tissue systems (dermal, ground, vascular) have their precursors (protoderm, ground meristem, procambium) formed during embryogenesis, so this is correct.  

Thus, the incorrect statement is **(C)**.  

Final answer: (C)
